source: J. J. Thomson, 'Cathode Rays', Philosophical Magazine (5th series) 44, 293-316 (1897), doi:10.1080/14786449708621070
transcription: Classic Chemistry transcription by Carmen J. Giunta, Le Moyne College: https://web.lemoyne.edu/~giunta/thomson1897.html (read 9 November 2026). Values typed exactly as printed there; the transcriber's mark [sic-CJG] on the last Tube 3 row is kept in 'note'.
units_as_printed: CGS electromagnetic (emu): m/e in g per abcoulomb, v in cm/s, W/Q in erg per abcoulomb, I = H*rho in gauss*cm, H in gauss (oersted), F in abvolt/cm, l in cm, theta in rad.
si_conversion: 1 abC = 10 C, 1 g = 1e-3 kg, so (m/e)_SI [kg/C] = 1e-4 * (m/e)_emu; v_SI = 1e-2 v_cgs; H 1 G -> B = 1e-4 T; F 1 abV/cm = 1e-8 V/cm = 1e-6 V/m; l 1 cm = 1e-2 m. Done in ref/ch01.py, never by hand.

method1_heat.what: Thermal method: cathode rays caught in an insulated cylinder (charge Q) and on a thermojunction (energy W); bent by a uniform field H with radius rho. m/e = I^2 Q / (2 W), v = 2 W / (Q I), I = H rho.
rows: transcriber marks the printed value 1.0 with [sic-CJG]
method1_heat.thomson_comment: Thomson judged the Tube 1 and 2 values too small because charge leaked from the inner cylinder through the ionised gas.

method2_crossed.what: Crossed-field method: plates of length l give deflection theta under electric intensity F; coils give the same deflection under H; theta = F (e/m) l / v^2, phi = H (e/m) l / v; with phi = theta: v = F/H, m/e = H^2 l / (F theta). Mean H over l was 60 x coil current.
rows: F printed as 1.x10^10 in the transcription
method2_crossed.apparatus: Plates (as printed) about 5 cm long, 2 cm broad, 1.5 cm apart.
